To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main factors related with the growth of the demand of international tourism are: the private investment on the tourism assets, the trade openness and the leisure tourism; and the growth of business tourism is not contagious.

the demand of international tourism is influenced by a country's own economic and tourism-related factors, but not by the demand of its neighbouring countries, which means that the demand is not contagious.

the demand of international tourism business is positively influenced by the private investment on the tourism assets, the demand of tourism for leisure purposes, the trade openness, the income per capita and the number of international flights.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the factors that influence international business tourism and the contagion effect that this demand may have in the surrounding areas.
the analysis of the determinants of international business tourism demand.
the factors that influence business tourism demand in countries worldwide, and the contagion effects of the demand of business and leisure tourism between neighbouring countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth of business tourism in one country is independent of the business tourism demand in its neighbouring countries.
business tourism is not a contagious phenomenon.
the main factors that influence the development of business tourism are those that influence the growth in the incomes of the countries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
countries with a high level of business tourism should invest in tourism infrastructures and services and should increase the number of tourists from other countries.
the demand of international tourism business in a country is determined by the demand of leisure tourism, the private investment on tourist assets, the trade openness and the level of income.
the demand of international tourism business in a country is influenced by its exogenous characteristics, but it is not influenced by the demand of neighbouring countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the demand of international tourism is not contagious.

tourism policies aimed at promoting the demand for international business tourism should focus on the development of the tourism assets and the increase in the trade openness, but not on the increase of the leisure tourism.
the tourism authorities should not focus only on the demand of business tourists but also on other factors that influence the demand of this kind of tourism.
